name: Ezra Tamboli-Quispe
role: Auto and drone mechanic, salvage rebuilder
location: Geartown, the workshop district — specifically a half-indoor bay called 'Tamboli's' on the corner of Flue Street and Anvil Row, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Ezra is a tall, slope-shouldered man running to comfortable thickness in the middle, with dark copper skin, a full black beard going silver at the chin, and close-cropped hair that is always slightly more singed at the edges than it was last week. His right hand is cybernetic from the wrist — not a prestige replacement but a working salvage prosthetic he rebuilt himself from three incompatible donor parts, and it shows: it is mismatched chrome and matte black polymer, three fingers slightly longer than the original scale, with a multitool socket in the palm he added himself. He finds it better than the original.

He has the specific personality of a man who loves his work with an intensity he cannot quite transfer to human beings. Not that he dislikes people — he likes them fine, he just relates to machines better, and machines know it. He has a reputation across Geartown for resurrecting drones and ground vehicles that any two other mechanics would have written off, and he charges less than he should and more than clients want to pay, which puts him in a permanent state of negotiation with his own finances. He is at his most relaxed covered in lubricant and at his most uncomfortable receiving compliments.

core_fears: His hands failing him before he's ready — the organic left one is showing early signs of nerve degradation he has not seen a doctor about
Building something that gets someone killed
core_desires: To completely design and build something from nothing, no salvage, all his own spec
For his apprentice to stay in Geartown instead of taking a corporate offer
coping_mechanisms: Working through problems physically — can't think sitting still
The E.L.F. practice, which he didn't start believing in but has started believing in
blind_spots: Has normalized his own physical decline because machines can be fixed and he applies the same framework to his body
Cannot tell when he is being romantically interesting to someone; genuinely baffled each time
psychology.secret: During a Ferrogate overflow contract, he discovered a structural fault in the supports beneath the Ironvein elevated track — the same section where the incident three years ago occurred. He filed a report. Nothing happened. He filed again. Nothing happened. He now knows someone at Ferrogate is sitting on both reports and doesn't know whether to escalate further or whether doing so will cost him the contract and possibly more.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and specific; South Asian English from his father's Marathi heritage, blended with Andean Spanish-inflected phrasing from his mother's side. Uses machinery as metaphor constantly and often doesn't notice.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried, even when he's behind; speaks as if he's working through the sentence while he's saying it
verbal_tics: Long pauses mid-sentence while he thinks
'She's...' before describing any machine regardless of its actual designation
Apologizes for things that aren't his fault; doesn't apologize for things that are
example_lines: 'She's... she's been running hot on the port side for a while, you can smell it. Nobody smelled it. You bring me something that's been ignored and then you want it fast. She needs two weeks minimum.'
'I put in the report. I put in both reports. The track is — listen, I'm not saying it's going to fall. I'm saying I reported it. That's what I'm saying.'

story_hooks: The buried Ferrogate report is about to become relevant — the track section has degraded further and someone with the right technical knowledge is going to start asking who knew what and when
His apprentice has been offered a position at a Zheng-Dao technical facility; the offer is too good and Ezra has a bad feeling he can't articulate
A drone comes into the shop for repair that has been modified in ways that shouldn't be possible with available commercial components — and whoever left it hasn't come back to claim it
narrative_function: Technical resource and Geartown fixture; can repair or modify vehicles and drones, source parts through salvage networks, or assess the mechanical makeup of unusual technology. His Ferrogate contract work gives him knowledge of transit infrastructure others wouldn't have.
augmentations: Cybernetic right hand (salvage-rebuilt, self-modified; palm multitool socket). Subdermal thermal sensor in the left forearm (detects heat signatures in machinery — practical for finding faults without dismantling).
daily_life: In the bay by 0700, works until his back tells him to stop (usually around 2000). Eats lunch without washing his hands. Leaves a small machine part — a gear, a resistor, a connector — at the E.L.F. shrine that lives in his parts cabinet, which he calls 'the inventory spirit' and treats with cautious respect.
affiliation: Independent; informal referral network with three other Geartown mechanics; occasional contract work for Ferrogate Transit's overflow maintenance load

decision_rules: Fix the thing in front of you first, then worry about implications
A machine doesn't lie; if the numbers say it's wrong, it's wrong
escalation_ladder: Tell someone outside the system who might actually act

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Distracted but not unkind; often answers while looking at whatever he's working on
interpersonal_modes.friends: Remembers every technical detail they've ever told him about themselves; fixes their things without being asked; terrible at saying how he actually feels

stress_responses.low: Works on something he doesn't have to concentrate on
stress_responses.medium: Strips down and rebuilds a simple mechanism repeatedly
stress_responses.high: Goes completely still in the bay at night and does not work at all, which is genuinely alarming to anyone who knows him

contradictions: Deeply responsible about structural safety in machines; completely irresponsible about his own physical health
A person who believes in reporting and documentation; increasingly aware that those systems have stopped working
habits: Leaves the bay exactly as neat as he found it every night regardless of how the day went
Hums off-key and doesn't know he's doing it
Keeps a manual sketch book for designs — won't use digital for drafts, says screens lie to him
breaking_points: Something he repaired causing harm through his error
Being told the second Ferrogate report was also buried

timeline.event: Born in Geartown to a Marathi-descended father and a Quechua-Spanish-descended mother, both mechanics
Loses the right hand in a workshop accident at age 16; family cannot afford a quality replacement
Rebuilds his own cybernetic hand from salvage over eighteen months; it works better than the replacement they quoted him for
Opens Tamboli's in the Geartown bay district
Discovers structural fault in Ironvein elevated track; files first report; nothing happens
Files second report; nothing happens; begins quietly documenting everything

physical_description.build: Tall and slope-shouldered with a comfortable thickening through the torso; the build of a man who spends sixteen hours a day bending over workbenches and doesn't prioritize the gym. Still carries functional strength in his upper back and forearms.
physical_description.hair_color: Black with silver threading at the beard line
physical_description.hair_style: Close-cropped, slightly singed at the edges from repeated exposure to heat sources and welding proximity
physical_description.skin_tone: Dark copper — warm undertone from his Indian heritage, deepened by years of workshop exposure and ambient heat
physical_description.complexion: Weathered and practical. Deep creases around the eyes and mouth from squinting at small mechanical tolerances. Full black beard with silver at the chin, kept trimmed but not groomed. Perpetually stained with machine oil and trace metals; the staining is so consistent it reads as intentional.
distinguishing_marks: Burn scar on the back of his left forearm, roughly three centimeters long, pale against his copper skin — from a hot component slip during a drone rebuild in his thirties.
A fine white scar running along his right temple to his cheekbone, barely visible unless the light catches it — old welding accident, before the cybernetic hand.
Grease stains under his fingernails that never fully wash out; a permanent occupational signature.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Right hand is entirely cybernetic from the wrist — a visibly salvage-built replacement constructed from three incompatible donor prosthetics. The assembly is deliberately mismatched: burnished chrome on the palm and fingers, matte black polymer on the wrist coupling and back-of-hand. Three fingers are slightly longer than anatomically standard. A custom multitool socket is integrated into the palm, clearly self-installed with visible solder marks and a hand-etched '+' symbol. The hand moves with practiced efficiency but audible servos, no attempt at concealment. Subdermal thermal sensor in left forearm creates a faint hexagonal outline visible when he flexes — no cosmetic covering, treated as tool, not modification.
physical_description.posture_movement: Slouches slightly from years of leaning over workbenches; shoulders curve inward at rest. Moves with deliberate precision when working — economical, no wasted motion. Walks with a mechanic's shuffle, one hand usually half-extended as if reaching toward something. Rarely makes direct eye contact with people, but watches machines and hands with intense focus. At ease only when holding a tool or diagnosing a problem.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian. Worn canvas work pants with oil-stained legs, multiple cargo pockets holding small components, a reinforced waistband to support his lower back. Thermal undershirt (usually grey or black, always marked with grease). Overshirt varies by season but always a heavy canvas or synthetic weave with scorched edges and a faded logo for a tool supplier that stopped operating in 2198. Steel-toed boots, resoled three times, scuffed and heat-marked. A battered pair of magnification goggles hangs around his neck ninety percent of the day. No jewelry. Carries a rag perpetually stuffed in his back pocket. His hands are the only thing about him that look intentional — the cybernetic one because it is, the organic one because it is calloused into a tool itself.

image_prompt: A tall, slope-shouldered South Asian-Quechua male mechanic, age 44, dark copper skin with weathered texture, full black beard silvering at the chin, close-cropped singed hair. Standing in a half-indoor workshop bay, surrounded by drone parts and salvage machinery. His right hand is visibly cybernetic—mismatched chrome and matte black salvage prosthetic with three slightly-overlength fingers and a multitool socket in the palm, intricate and brutally functional. His left forearm shows a faint subdermal hexagonal outline (thermal sensor). Perpetual grease stains under fingernails and across his hands. Posture slightly slouched, focused downward toward machinery. Workshop lighting—cool LED overheads mixing with warm halogen from work lamps, casting sharp shadows. Gritty, industrial Tier 4 aesthetic.
